newsitem.title: USA: Stanford University Rev Rfdg Bnds Rtd AAA/A-.
newsitem.headline: Stanford University Rev Rfdg Bnds Rtd AAA/A-.

text.p: NEW YORK, Oct 17 - Standard & Poor's today has assigned its triple-A'/A-1'-plus rating to California Educational Facilities Authority's $8.775 million refunding revenue bonds series L-4, issued for Stanford University.
Also, Standard & Poor's has affirmed its outstanding ratings on debt issued for the university, as indicated in the list below.
The triple-A' rating on Stanford University's long-term debt reflects Stanford's
-- Pre-eminent status among U.S. universities,
-- Extremely strong student demand profile,
-- Solid financial performance, and
-- Large endowment fund balances.

The A-1'-plus short-term rating indicates strong levels of internal liquidity, consisting primarily of Stanford's expendable funds pool, sufficient to cover any optional tenders. This variable-rate debt issuance is the forth of a series expected to total $50 million through fiscal 1999. Bond proceeds will refund earlier revenue bond issues and essentially roll current maturities out an additional 20 years.

Located in Palo Alto, just south of San Francisco, Stanford is one of the premier comprehensive research institutions in the U.S. University enrollment is evenly split between undergraduate and graduate, with fall 1996 enrollment totaling just over 13,000. Undergraduate demand has recovered strongly, after experiencing declines that the university attributed to the Loma Prieta earthquake in 1990. Since that time, freshman applications have rebounded 25% to total 16,359.

As a result, selectivity has improved further, as just 16% of those who applied were granted admission for fall 1996. In addition, an impressive 61% matriculated, up from Stanford's historical levels in the mid-50% range. Just over 40% of the freshman class is from California, followed by Texas, New York, Washington, Illinois, and Oregon. Student quality is quite high, with 96% of entering students in the top-20% of their high school class, and 75% and 91% of incoming students exceeding 600 on the verbal and math portions of the SAT, respectively. Undergraduate tuition is nearly $20,490, with total costs of $28,000. Financial aid expenditures remain modest, demonstrated by a tuition discount rate of 14%.

Currently, Stanford has over $4 billion of assets under the direction of the Stanford Management Co. (SMC). Of this total, over $1.4 billion can be considered unrestricted and $1.1 billion is invested in highly liquid assets. For the purpose of this issue, Standard & Poor's is focusing primarily on the most liquid portion of the school's assets, since Stanford has chosen to issue this variable-rate debt unenhanced, backed solely by the university's own liquidity. Combining the $200 million authorization for the commercial paper program ($108 million currently outstanding) and the expected $50 million of unenhanced variable-rate debt to be issued through 1999, the university has demonstrated strong historical liquidity coverage of over four times. As part of its five-year capital plan, Stanford plans $708 million of capital projects -- two-thirds for renovation and one-third for new construction. The university has identified funding sources for one-half of the capital plan, and expects the remainder to be funded through additional debt and gifts. Additional debt will be supported by various auxiliary facilities and a 0.5% supplement to the 4.75% endowment spending rate. Debt outstanding totals $730 million, and maximum annual debt service totals $73 million, or 5% of overall expenses.
OUTLOOK: Stable.

The outlook on Stanford's long-term debt rating reflects Standard & Poor's expectation that student demand will remain strong, current levels of unrestricted monies will be maintained, and that management will achieve success in its administrative restructuring, Standard & Poor's said. --
RATINGS AFFIRMED California Educational Facilities Authority $23.67 mil. rfdg. rev. bnds. ser. L-1, L-2, and L-3 AAA/A-1+
$314.2 mil. ser. B, C, H-K AAA
Stanford University $150 mil. med.-term nts. ser. A AAA
$150 mil. 6.875% taxable bnds. due 2024 AAA
$30 mil. taxable nts. AAA
$200 mil. taxable CP A-1+
